themes_detail.label: Dead Animals Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints spiked to 9 reports THIS WEEK, up 380% from the 8-week average of 1.9 per week (z-score: 9.13), suggesting a potential disease vector, environmental contamination, or pest infestation problem requiring immediate public health investigation.
evidence: 9 dead animal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
380% increase with z-score of 9.13 (statistically severe anomaly)
Timing coincides with warmer spring weather and potential pest breeding conditions
reporting_angles: Contact DSNY and NYC Department of Health to determine if spike correlates to known disease outbreak, pest infestation, or wildlife disruption in CD 309
Interview residents in affected blocks about visible animal carcasses, odors, and health concerns; cross-reference 311 complaint addresses for geographic clustering

themes_detail.label: Traffic Congestion Surge
themes_detail.summary: Traffic complaints jumped to 7 reports LAST WEEK, up 409% from the 8-week average of 1.4 per week (z-score: 3.57), indicating a possible new traffic pattern, infrastructure failure, or event-driven congestion in Flatbush/Park Slope.
evidence: 7 traffic complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Timing aligns with spring break and potential for increased deliveries; warrants comparison to DOT incident reports
reporting_angles: Obtain detailed 311 complaint addresses and times to map whether congestion is concentrated on specific corridors (e.g., Flatbush Ave, Prospect Park SW)
Cross-reference with DOT/NYPD incident data, construction permits (365 filed in last 90 days), and for-hire vehicle uptick (243% increase last week) to identify root cause

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Complaints
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints reached 3 LAST WEEK, up 243% from the 8-week average of 0.9 per week (z-score: 6.43), suggesting surge in Uber/Lyft activity, unsafe driving, or conflicts with residents and traditional taxis.
evidence: 3 for-hire vehicle complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Correlates with traffic spike (7 complaints last week) and historical Flatbush congestion concerns
reporting_angles: Interview residents and local business owners about increase in double-parking, blocking driveways, and aggressive driving by rideshare vehicles
Request TLC data on for-hire vehicle pickups/dropoffs in CD 309 over past month; compare to traditional taxi complaints

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Outbreak 2 Weeks Ago
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked to 22 reports TWO WEEKS AGO, up 780% from the 8-week average of 2.5 per week (z-score: 8.13), representing a coordinated or gang-related tagging campaign or community neglect that may still be visible.
evidence: 22 graffiti complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 2.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
780% spike with z-score of 8.13 (second-highest severity signal after dead animals)
Spike has cooled since 2 weeks ago but suggests active crew or gang activity in specific neighborhood corridors
reporting_angles: Identify geographic clusters of graffiti complaints from 2 weeks ago; visit affected blocks to see if tags remain and assess cleanup response
Contact NYPD about any known gang tags or crews active in Flatbush/PLG; interview Parks/Sanitation about graffiti removal timeline

themes_detail.label: Unleashed Dog Incidents
themes_detail.summary: Unleashed dog complaints hit 3 reports TWO WEEKS AGO, up 1100% from the 8-week average of 0.2 per week (z-score: 6.35), indicating a serious public safety concern around aggressive or uncontrolled animals in parks and neighborhoods.
evidence: 3 unleashed dog complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
1100% spike with z-score of 6.35 (fifth-highest severity signal)
Pattern suggests either owner negligence in parks (Prospect Park, Parade Grounds) or wider off-leash dog culture emerging
reporting_angles: Interview residents near Prospect Park, Parade Grounds, and neighborhood parks about encounters with aggressive unleashed dogs; assess if incidents involved injuries
Contact Parks Department about off-leash dog enforcement; determine if there are recurring offenders or hotspot parks with inadequate supervision
